'''''Ulva compressa''''' is a species of [[seaweed]] in [[Ulvaceae]] family that can be found in [[North America]], [[Mediterranean Sea]], and throughout [[Africa]] and [[Australia]].<ref name=seaweedindustry>{{cite web|url=https://seaweedindustry.com/seaweed/type/ulva-compressa|title=Ulva compressa|publisher=Seaweed Industry|access-date=March 24, 2013|archive-date=March 31, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140331225402/https://seaweedindustry.com/seaweed/type/ulva-compressa|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Description==
The species is green coloured and is measured {{convert|2|-|20|cm}} in length.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.flora.sa.gov.au/efsa/algae_revealed/pdf/Enteromorpha_compressa.pdf|title= Enteromorpha (Ulva) compressa (Linnaeus) Greville|access-date=March 24, 2013}}</ref>

== Distribution ==
This species is widespread worldwide including in the North and South Atlantic and in the Pacific Ocean.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=New Zealand seaweeds : an illustrated guide|last=W. A.|first=Nelson|publisher=Te Papa Press|year=2013|isbn=9780987668813|location=Wellington, New Zealand|pages=42|oclc=841897290|author-link=Wendy Nelson (marine scientist)}}</ref>

==Habitat==
The species can be found  in the intertidal zone in sheltered to open coastal sites, in shallow water, [[tide pool]]s, and also on [[rock pool]]s and [[sand]].<ref name=seaweedindustry/><ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.seaweed.ie/descriptions/ulva_compressa.php|title=Ulva compressa Linnaeus|access-date=March 24, 2013|archive-date=January 16, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130116032251/http://www.seaweed.ie/descriptions/ulva_compressa.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Consumption and production==
The plant is widely produced in [[China]], [[Japan]], and [[Korea]]. The species is edible by both [[animal]]s and [[human]]s alike, due to its high levels of nutrients and good taste. It is also used in  various cosmetics to prevent skin itchiness. It is used as [[fertilizer]] because it adds a wide range of [[mineral]]s to the [[soil]].<ref name=seaweedindustry/>
